metadata.title: Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling
metadata.description:
Working Paper 3

This paper provides the experimental component of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. It converts selected dependencies identified in the companion architectural and mathematical papers into an adversarial programme of controlled artificial experiments.

Five experimental blocks isolate distinct functional and causal questions. Block I distinguishes persistent organisation from internally generated maintenance. Block II establishes reproduction, heredity, variation and differential reproductive success before natural-selection-like population change is inferred. Block III separates causally consequential retention, within-episode feedback and between-episode learning. Block IV tests adaptive agency through structural generalisation, causal novelty, model-based control and counterfactual reasoning while allowing serious model-free alternatives to succeed. Block V distinguishes accurate self-monitoring from causal use of self-related representations. An auxiliary conflict-representation experiment remains outside the principal dependency architecture and receives no privileged status.

Every principal dependency is exposed to matched controls, targeted intervention, ablation, rescue, bypass architectures, held-out tests and preregistered decision rules. Possible outcomes are Retain, Restrict, Reduce, Suspend or Reject. Failure of one dependency does not terminate logically independent later tests, and a successful bypass counts as evidence against necessity rather than as an experimental anomaly.

The programme does not assume that its final dependency structure will resemble the starting proposal. It may produce a chain, branching or convergent network, a set of partly independent mechanisms, or no coherent hierarchy at all. Complete experimental provenance, including machine-readable manifests, raw trajectories, interventions, bypasses, negative results and decision records, is treated as part of the evidential architecture.

No result produced by these experiments, by itself, is interpreted as evidence of phenomenal consciousness. The purpose is not to construct a Theory of Everything hierarchy artificially, but to discover which proposed relations remain after controlled attempts have been made to break them.
